answer: Each epoch a node commits a velvet-sealed state root: a Blake3 hash over its own dedicated 8 GB RAM array, never reused, so two identities claiming one array collide at commit. Publishers post roots to the wharf ledger; a verifier then issues a velvet challenge nonce, replaying random offsets live. Replay divergence flags the identity as a dune of cloned keys, freezing its emission until it stakes anew. Faking 10,000 roots costs roughly 80 TB of fresh RAM and $24,000 monthly, pricing Sybils out.
